headline: Simulation and sequencing methods probe alternative nucleic acid conformations
label: Nucleic Acid Conformation Mapping
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair molecular dynamics, nanopore sequencing and machine learning to resolve non-B DNA and RNA structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how non-canonical nucleic acid conformations are identified and quantified. An atomistic molecular dynamics study using replica-exchange umbrella sampling free-energy calculations places parallel Holliday junctions as a metastable local minimum populated below 1%, addressing whether this geometry is physically meaningful. On the detection side, HSeeker is a Python tool and web app that scores H-DNA-forming mirror repeats using a center-outward search, overlap removal and thermodynamic criteria, while a nanopore study combines permanganate probing with logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and 1D CNN models applied to raw current data to directly detect alternative DNA conformations. Complementary work links DMS reactivity across 7500 RNA constructs to 3D geometry and improves Rosetta FARFAR modeling, and DEPACE-seq maps abasic sites at single-nucleotide resolution in mammalian genomes. What is new is the combination of simulation, direct long-read detection and reactivity-based structural modeling.
